sections.title: Delete my account handler
sections.what: Checks the request body, deletes the signed-in user's account through the account service, and returns an empty success response.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the user's right to remove their own data.
sections.watch_out: The parsed body is thrown away after the check, so the confirmation it asks for is not used by the delete step.

summary: Lets a signed-in user delete their own account.
purpose: Meets the need for users to remove their data.
why: Likely reason: deleting an account is a privacy right, and the route is the entry point for it.
how: 1) Confirms sign-in. 2) Checks the body against the delete schema. 3) Calls the delete function for this user. 4) Returns an empty success response.
inputs: A POST with a JSON body checked against the delete schema. The user comes from the session.
outputs: An empty 204 response when the account is deleted.
risks: The checked body is then ignored, so any confirmation it asks for is enforced only by its shape. Whether deletion is permanent is not visible here.
debug: If deletion fails, check the delete schema and the delete function in the account service.
